{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --time=12:00:00
#   --gres=gpu:k20:0
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem=4G
#   -o ./results/slurm-%A_%a.out

flux alloc \
  -n 1 \
  -c 1 \
  --time=12h \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p ./results

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=4G has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --gres=gpu:k20:0 explicitly requests 0 GPUs of type k20.
# This is preserved by NOT requesting GPUs in Flux.
# Performance implication: if the workload actually needs a GPU, it will not have one allocated.

# NOTE: Slurm output pattern uses %A/%a (array job/task ids). Flux has no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but log naming/organization may be degraded.
# Best-effort: write to a single file named with Flux job id.
exec >"./results/slurm-${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

module load imkl/2018.3.222
module load openmpi/3.1.2
module load cuda/10.0.130
module load python/3.7

source /project/cq-training-1/project1/teams/team06/ift6759-env/bin/activate
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:/cvmfs/soft.computecanada.ca/easybuild/software/2017/avx2/Compiler/intel2016.4/cuda/10.0.130/extras/CUPTI/lib64

python evaluator.py predictions.txt data/admin_cfg.json -u data/user_cfg.json
'
"
}
